title: Cap. VI Arg. 10: Augustine and Prosper — depth of grace not opened by free choice
pass_a_gloss: But far otherwise holy Augustine, Against Two Letters of the Pelagians, book 4, chapter 6: Why he makes these sheep, and those not, with whom there is no respect of persons, that itself is the question which pertains to that height, etc. And Prosper, On the Calling of the Gentiles, book 1, chapter 23: In vain do they try to open the depth of inscrutable grace through free choice, who set the cause of election in the merits of those who are elected. And in the last chapter: The depth of that question, which according to the Apostle's admiration we confess unsearchable, is not solved by the willing and not-willing of free choice.
pass_b_english: Far otherwise Augustine (Against Two Letters of the Pelagians 4.6): why he makes these sheep and not those — with whom there is no respect of persons — that very question belongs to that height. And Prosper (On the Calling of the Gentiles 1.23): in vain they try to open the depth of inscrutable grace by free choice, who plant election's cause in the merits of the elect. And in the last chapter: that question's depth, which with the Apostle's wonder we confess unsearchable, is not solved by free choice's willing and refusing.
source_text: At longe aliter sanctus Augustinus Contr. 2. Epistol. Pelag. lib. 4. cap. 6: Quare istos oves facit, et istos non facit, apud quem non est acceptio personarum, ipsa est quaestio quae pertinet ad illam altitudinem, etc. Et Prosper, De vocat. gent. lib. 1. cap. 23: Frustra profunditatem inscrutabilis gratiae per liberum arbitrium conantur aperire, qui causam electionis in eorum constituunt meritis qui eliguntur. Et cap. ultimo: Profunditas illius quaestionis, quam secundum admirationem Apostoli impervestigabilem confitemur, per liberi arbitrii velle et nolle non solvitur.
